questionText: How do you record a spam filter in an AI inventory?

answerOptions.text: Record product, exact filter function, version, purpose, data and owner; check the technical and legal classification against evidence.
Count every spam filter as a standalone AI system without review.
Record the provider only; function and version do not matter.
Never record spam filters, because email cannot be an AI use case.

explanation: The product name says neither how the version works nor how it is classified in law. Into the inventory goes the function, the vendor documentation and the assessing unit.

questionText: You want to draft a private text with an AI assistant. Which selection rule holds?

answerOptions.text: Only paid business tools may be used to write text.
A service can fit if you may share the content and its data controls, retention and terms suit the purpose.
Only the best-known product, because a brand determines security.
No AI tool may be used to write text.

explanation: Private raises the same questions: content, rights, data controls, retention, terms. Price and brand are not security classes. And credentials belong in no prompt.

questionText: A colleague uses suggested replies, a transcription function and a route forecast. What follows for certain?

answerOptions.text: None of the functions can contain AI.
Exactly one function is AI, whatever the product and version.
That is automatically exactly three standalone AI systems in law.
The concrete functions and versions belong in the inventory; their classification has to be checked.

explanation: Three product names, and still no count of standalone AI systems. AI-supported functions sit embedded in everyday products. Function and version get recorded; the review comes after.

questionText: Why does a maintained inventory of the AI functions and systems in use matter?

answerOptions.text: It is needed for the tax return.
A maintained inventory creates a reviewable basis for risk assessment, rules and ownership.
It is mandatory only for companies with more than 250 employees.
Its sole purpose is IT budget planning.

explanation: No inventory, no risk assessment, no ownership, no approval that holds. It is a governance building block. Whether it is legally required, and in which form, depends on the concrete system and role.

questionText: An employee wants to process a customer list with names and email addresses in an unapproved AI service. Which statement holds?

answerOptions.text: Business contact details are always unrestricted.
A paid account is legal basis enough.
Processing stops until purpose, legal basis, data class, minimization and the concrete system approval are settled.
Digitally stored data may not be processed.

explanation: Names and email addresses can be personal data. A DPA alone does not make the processing lawful. Purpose, legal basis, minimization, contract, configuration and the organizational approval belong to it.

questionText: Which basis is enough to approve an AI workflow?

answerOptions.text: The product name contains the word Enterprise.
The documented review of purpose, data class, product feature, contract, configuration, permissions and retention.
The provider excludes customer data from training by default.
The system runs on a local machine.

explanation: An approval covers a concrete combination: purpose, data, feature, configuration. Contract, permissions, retention, region and further duties have to fit. "Enterprise" in the name checks nothing. A local machine neither.

questionText: Why must unapproved consumer offers not be used with company data?

answerOptions.text: Because their answers are worse than the paid versions.
Because a reviewed contract, binding data controls and a documented approval are usually missing.
Because they work in English only.
Because they need no internet connection.

explanation: With unapproved consumer offers the organization usually lacks a reviewed DPA, binding data controls and an agreed data region. With personal company data the use can therefore be unlawful. What that looks like depends on purpose, legal basis, contract and configuration.

questionText: A colleague wants to analyse a supplier list with company names, contacts and purchasing terms. Which statement holds?

answerOptions.text: That is allowed as soon as an enterprise product is used.
That is always prohibited, whatever the purpose and the approved specialist workflow.
Purpose, personal data, confidentiality, minimization and the approved workflow have to be checked before input.
Supplier data may never go into an AI tool.

explanation: One list, three kinds of data. The company name can be public, the contact can mean personal data, the terms can be a trade secret. The concrete approval of purpose, data and system decides.

questionText: What is the main difference between a good prompt and a bad one?

answerOptions.text: A good prompt is longer than 500 words.
A usable prompt names task, relevant inputs, wanted format, limits and how to handle missing information.
A good prompt uses English technical terms.
A good prompt always starts with 'Please'.

explanation: Clear inputs and clear limits make the output checkable. The role description is optional, and even a precise prompt guarantees neither correctness nor completeness.

questionText: You use an AI assistant to write an email to an important customer. The generated text sounds professional. What is your next step?

answerOptions.text: Send it at once, AI assistants make no mistakes in emails.
Check facts and sources, completeness, your authority, the audience and any required approval.
Have a second AI tool check the text.
Send the email next week to gain some distance.

explanation: Any draft can sound professional. That establishes nothing and authorizes nothing. The control follows the impact: sources, gaps, commitments, data, audience. A second AI tool is no review.

questionText: Which constraint should a good prompt for an email template carry?

answerOptions.text: 'Use only the supplied facts, mark gaps, and add no unauthorized commitments'.
'Write at least 1,000 words'.
'Use emojis to sound friendly'.
'Include as many technical terms as possible'.

explanation: The constraint makes visible what the assistant invented and keeps commitments small. Approval of the input data it does not replace. Specialist review neither.

questionText: You ask an AI assistant to turn your meeting notes into minutes. The output carries a point that was never discussed. What do you do?

answerOptions.text: Keep the point, because the AI assistant may have caught something you missed.
Check the point against the primary source, remove unsupported content and tighten the prompt for the next draft.
Discard the whole record and write the minutes by hand.
Put a question mark on the point and send it to everyone.

explanation: Models sometimes add what the source does not carry. A tighter instruction makes that rarer, not impossible. The source comparison stays.

questionText: What is an AI hallucination?

answerOptions.text: A technical system error in which the AI crashes.
A plausible-sounding output that is unsupported or wrong.
Deliberate manipulation by hackers.
A visual error in the user interface.

explanation: A language model produces token sequences. A fact check does not run along automatically. Every claim a decision hangs on goes back to a suitable source.

questionText: Copilot writes a market analysis with the claim: 'The German AI market grew by 34.2% to EUR 12.8 billion in 2025 (source: Bitkom 2025).' How do you check that?

answerOptions.text: The figure sounds plausible, that is enough.
Open the Bitkom website and look for the study named.
Ask ChatGPT whether the figure is right.
Replace the figure with your own estimate.

explanation: Figure, percentage, citation: all of it can be generated without the study existing. Open the named primary source and check definition, period and calculation. Asking ChatGPT is the same error source again.

questionText: Which use needs specialist and organizational controls beyond a simple output review?

answerOptions.text: Writing an internal newsletter piece.
Legal assessments, medical recommendations or decisions with significant consequences for people.
Translating an email from German into English.
Building an agenda for a team meeting.

explanation: Newsletter, translation, agenda: the simple review does it. Legal, medical and employment decisions carry heavy consequences and need qualified accountability, suitable sources and special oversight controls.

questionText: Copilot summarises a 45-minute Teams meeting. The summary records: 'The team agreed to start the project on 1 June.' You remember the date stayed open. What follows?

answerOptions.text: Copilot is probably right, because it analysed the whole audio.
The date is unsupported; compare it with the transcript or confirmed notes and keep it open.
The date was probably discussed while you were briefly distracted.
Copilot invents no concrete dates, so the date is right.

explanation: Memory against summary. Neither is primary evidence. Check the approved source and have the participants confirm the record. Until then the date stays open.

questionText: Which of the following belongs in an AI usage policy?

answerOptions.text: A technical explanation of how neural networks work.
An approval matrix with purpose, product version and feature, data classes, configuration, owners and review status.
The full original text of the EU AI Act.
Instructions for programming AI models.

explanation: No lecture on neural networks, no legal text, no programming course. A policy describes approvals as a combination of purpose, feature, data and configuration, plus review duties, incident reporting and ownership.

questionText: What does Article 4 of the EU AI Act require from companies that use AI systems?

answerOptions.text: That every employee holds a university degree in computer science.
That providers and deployers take measures supporting the development of AI literacy in people acting on their behalf, and consider the prescribed context.
That only IT departments may use AI systems.
That companies commission an annual AI audit by external auditors.

explanation: Article 4 has applied since 2 February 2025. As amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 it requires measures supporting the development of AI literacy, taking account of technical knowledge, experience, education and training, use context and the people affected. No degree, no IT monopoly, no annual audit, no prescribed attestation.

questionText: An employee accidentally enters payroll data into an AI service. What is the correct first response?

answerOptions.text: Wait and see whether anyone notices.
Delete the chat history and tell nobody.
Use the published incident channel at once, preserve evidence, and leave the risk assessment to the responsible functions.
Ask the provider for a legal assessment and report nothing internally.

explanation: Report it, at once, through the internal channel. Evidence stays as it is. Whether a personal data breach exists and is notifiable is assessed by the controller. Internal four- or 24-hour stages are the organization's business, not the law's.

questionText: A new AI tool, an industry-specific chatbot say, is to be introduced. The AI usage policy already exists. What has to happen?

answerOptions.text: Nothing, the existing policy covers all new tools automatically.
Before use, purpose, features, data, contract, configuration, risks and owners are reviewed, and inventory and approval matrix are updated.
The tool may be trialled with real data until the next review.
Only the IT department is informed, the policy stays unchanged.

explanation: A new product is a review trigger. A new feature too. The organization assesses the workflow and records the decision before real data goes in.
